title: Responsive images with srcset and sizes
when: Images are heavy on phones, blurry on high density screens, or the user wants modern formats with fallbacks.
inputs: the images and where they appear
the widths they are displayed at
prompt:
Goal: Each image downloads at the size it is shown, stays sharp on dense screens, and never shifts the layout.
Steps:
1. Export each image at a few widths (for example 480, 800, 1200, 1600) named photo-480.jpg and so on.
2. Use srcset with width descriptors: srcset="photo-480.jpg 480w, photo-800.jpg 800w, photo-1200.jpg 1200w".
3. Write sizes to match the layout: sizes="(min-width: 64em) 33vw, 100vw" for a three column grid.
4. For modern formats use <picture> with <source type="image/avif"> and <source type="image/webp"> before the jpg img fallback.
5. Always set width, height (the intrinsic ratio), alt, and loading="lazy" plus decoding="async" for images below the first screen.
6. Use <picture> with media only for art direction (a different crop on phones).
Quality bar:
- Phones download the small file.
- No layout shift while images load.
- The hero image is not lazy loaded.
Pitfalls:
- sizes left out, so the browser assumes 100vw everywhere.
- Only one huge file listed in srcset.
- Forgetting the fallback img inside picture.
Verify:
- [ ] Every img has alt, width and height.
- [ ] srcset lists real files that exist.
- [ ] Images below the first screen are lazy.
- [ ] sizes matches the CSS layout.
Output: Updated HTML image markup and the list of image files needed per width.

examples.input: as fotos da galeria estão pesadas no celular
examples.output: picture with webp source and jpg fallback, srcset 480w to 1600w, sizes for a 3 column grid
